text:
Sam B.: Heads up: new user reported that the Go generator example leaks goroutines when you cancel the context mid-stream. Quick repro: start generator, read one token, cancel ctx. The iterator never returns until server-side finished.

Sam B.: Minimal snippet used to repro:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter, _ := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() {
  for {
    tok, err := iter.Next()
    if err != nil { break }
    fmt.Println(tok.Text)
  }
}()
// cancel immediately
cancel()
// expect goroutine to exit quickly
```

Lina K.: Oof. Which transport? http or grpc?

Sam B.: http in the sample app. I poked the SDK: it looks like the auth refresh/retry path restarts the request when the canceled request gets a 401 race. That reopens the stream and the previous reader goroutine is still stuck reading the body.

Ravi P.: That matches my local. For streaming we should not auto-retry, or at least the retry logic needs to be aware of ctx.Done(). Right now retry is transport-level and oblivious to iter lifecycle.

Ellen W.: Parity note: python/node SDKs cancel the stream immediately on ctx cancel or stream.close(). Go's generator iterator didn't implement Close well when we initially shipped. We should make the iterator implement io.Closer and guarantee Close cancels underlying request context and returns context.Canceled to in-flight Next() calls.

Lina K.: Suggested short-term changes: update sample app to call `defer iter.Close()` and change read loop to select on ctx.Done() as well. Long-term: SDK changes so streaming calls set a per-call meta `no_stream_retries: true` and the transport honors that.

Sam B.: I've opened a draft PR for the sample app that adds `defer iter.Close()` and a small example showing `select { case <-ctx.Done(): iter.Close(); return }` in the read loop. Link when ready.

Ravi P.: For the SDK patch I can add the Close() method and wire it to cancel the request context. Also add a small sentinel error mapping so callers see context.Canceled. Will include unit tests asserting Next() returns quickly after Close().

Ellen W.: Can we add a CI regression test that measures goroutine delta? e.g., snapshot runtime.NumGoroutine() before and after with a short timeout. If delta > 2 after Close() within 200ms fail the test. Those catch leaks pretty well.

Sam B.: Good idea. Also add a NOTE in Quickstart docs: "Streaming: respect ctx cancel or call Close() to avoid background goroutines." New users keep tripping over this in onboarding.

Lina K.: One more UX thought: consider making the iterator a boxed struct that exposes `Next(ctx context.Context)` as an alternative so the caller can pass a per-call ctx for cancellation semantics (instead of relying only on the parent ctx). Might simplify patterns.

Ravi P.: That API change could be additive: keep Next() for backward compatibility and add NextWithCtx(ctx). But prefer Close + parent ctx first to get safety quickly.

devx-bot: Created issue #2199: "go-sdk: generator streaming cancel/closes + transport retry race" and added labels: bug, ux, priority-high. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/2199 :robot_face:

Sam B.: I'll land the sample fix this afternoon and add the Quickstart note. Ravi, ping when your branch is ready and I'll run the leak test matrix locally.

Ellen W.: Thanks team. After patch lands, we should push a small release note so onboarding emails/quickstart links point to the updated example.

Lina K.: Agreed. Also capture follow-ups: expose buffer limits/backpressure, consider NextWithCtx ergonomic variant, and evaluate default retry policy for stream calls.

Sam B.: Sounds good. I'll create follow-up issues after the immediate fix. Thanks!
